Find the problem.

blocks.body: The official State Audit Office page/PDF did not load; its findings were read through BMG, not verified against the original. Open the official link in Sources, search for EMR/EHR compatibility and reporting gaps, and paste the relevant paragraphs with: Run Steps 1 to 4 again with this.

Problem: patient information and hospital work do not always connect, making coordination and reliable reporting harder.
Who: Georgian private multi-specialty hospitals and groups; owner/CEO buys, clinical/operations staff champion, finance and IT evaluate.
Search: Georgian and English; Georgia the country, not the US state.
Pain words: incomplete records, handoffs, repeated entry, reporting, documentation and reimbursement corrections.
Workarounds: spreadsheets, calls and manual checks are hypotheses unless a source identifies them.
Alternatives: existing hospital systems, add-on reporting and manual coordination; no unverified competitor install claims.
Exclude: patients' private experiences, non-hospital businesses, institutions outside supportable scope and tariff problems software cannot solve.
Scope: Phase 1 connected base system first; workflow AI and the proactive brain are later, separately agreed phases.

blocks.title: What this research actually found
blocks.body: Seven relevant source records, not 20 qualifying posts. Two historical executive interviews; four related C/Can project pages; one audit news report. Five named research contacts, but zero fully verified current purchase opportunities. Project participation is not an individual's statement of pain, and related project pages are not independent demand signals.

MediMind, medimind.md. Your 8 October explainer and 22 September buyer-pain research were used, with your later Phase 1 clarification taking precedence over older AI-inclusive copy. Your anchor agreement covers GeoHospitals' 25-hospital network with staged implementation; it is not proof of 25 independent wins or measured outcome improvement. This exercise prepares discovery only. No messages were sent.

Founder offer: for the next 10 hospital clients, an included parallel base-system evaluation before purchase commitment; current software stays in place. Price matching and continuing base-product development have agreed scope and written terms. About two weeks is a target after readiness, not an unconditional launch guarantee.

blocks.title: Recency rule
blocks.body: The preferred 90-day window is 14 July to 12 October 2026. An undated live page is not a recent post. Publication dates in articles were checked separately from site headers and search-engine crawl dates. Neither executive pain interview below falls inside that window.

Method: open original pages when available; paraphrase, do not invent quotes or roles; inspect official hospital sites for fit. Exclude personal patient reviews, international look-alikes and generic vendor claims from lead evidence. A linked employer or project is not a warm introduction.

blocks.title: How to use the network
blocks.body: Hypothesis: ask your existing clinical and 500 network whether anyone genuinely knows these professionals. C/Can is a public relationship map, not evidence you have a connection. Never claim a referral that did not happen. A clinician can help surface a problem; purchasing still needs an accountable hospital sponsor.

No direct professional invitation or verified personal contact channel was found for these five. No email addresses were guessed. Roles from undated C/Can pages need confirmation. The queue is ordered for practical discovery, not by independently measured pain severity.

blocks.body: Static project pages are not normal reply threads. Use these only after a genuine introduction or a verified invitation to professional contact. They are not instructions to post a comment or send an unsolicited personal message.

blocks.title: Todua | Maka Maglakelidze
blocks.body: C/Can lists you on its Tbilisi quality cancer management team. When a patient's diagnosis, treatment plan and follow-up involve different departments, which part of keeping everyone working from the same information takes the most effort today?

blocks.title: American Hospital Tbilisi | Natia Jokhadze
blocks.body: I saw your name on C/Can's Tbilisi quality cancer management project. How does your team prepare the full patient picture for a treatment discussion when information comes from several departments?

blocks.title: Caucasus Medical Centre | Ivane Kiladze
blocks.body: C/Can lists you in its Tbilisi care-quality project. What have you tried to make patient-information handoffs between diagnostic and treatment teams easier, and what still needs manual coordination?

blocks.title: Mardaleishvili | Nia Sharikadze
blocks.body: I came across the C/Can quality cancer management project you lead. Which coordination problem remains hardest to solve inside a hospital, rather than through changes to the wider health system?

blocks.title: Heart Centre | Archil Chukhrukidze, only after role confirmation
blocks.body: In your 2023 BMG interview, you discussed uncertainty around documentation-related inspections. Is assembling reliable documentation still a practical challenge for your team, and how do you handle it today?

blocks.title: What to listen for
blocks.body: One recent example. How often it repeats. Who does the extra work. What it costs in time or money. What they have tried. Why changing the current system is difficult. Ask for process examples, not identifiable patient records.

Across the seven records, coordination appears in two related C/Can pages; registry data quality appears in two related pages; policy/reimbursement, enforcement/documentation and electronic reporting each appear in one record. These are overlapping institutional sources, not seven independent buyer interviews. Financial loss, repeat entry and spreadsheet work remain hospital-specific hypotheses, not quantified findings.

pages.title: Turn learning into a real test
pages.subtitle: What to change and Final check | A proposed next step, not a forecast

blocks.title: Targeting hypothesis
blocks.body: Prioritise hospital workflow owners connected to real improvement programmes, then confirm a recurring internal problem. Multi-specialty hospitals remain the main market; specialised oncology is a separate hypothesis. Keep public-system contacts as research/connector possibilities, not paying-hospital leads.

blocks.title: Positioning hypothesis
blocks.body: Lead with keeping patient information and cross-team work connected. Test whether the buyer cares most about a slower handoff, hard-to-trust reporting or costly documentation corrections. Do not assume every reimbursement shortfall is caused by software. Avoid claiming full replacement is the only way any AI can work.

blocks.title: Offer hypothesis
blocks.body: Begin with one workflow walkthrough and a baseline. If there is enough fit, agree a limited Phase 1 parallel evaluation within the next-ten offer: named hospital reviewers, scope, data permission, success criteria and a decision date. This tests the broader replacement; it is not an autonomous-AI pilot.

blocks.title: Suggested journey
blocks.body:
Fit-check hospital -> genuine route in -> confirm recurring pain -> identify sponsor and champion -> agree scope, hospital approvals and permitted data -> launch parallel base system -> staff test it -> compare results -> purchase decision -> staged rollout.

Data permission and delivery are separate milestones. A launched environment is not a completed hands-on evaluation, a qualified lead or a sale.

Proposed first cycle: five genuine introductions/permission checks, three completed workflow conversations, one evaluation plan if fit is confirmed. These are proposed activity targets, not predicted conversion rates. Your working outcome metric remains new hospital buying organisations beyond the anchor partner completing their first hands-on parallel-system evaluation in the last 30 days.

Verdict: there is public evidence of local coordination and data-quality gaps, but not yet a verified set of current hospital buyers asking for our replacement.
Assumptions: Georgian private hospitals remain the first market; repeatable sales are not established by the anchor agreement; programme participants may be useful research contacts; oncology may be a supportable adjacent segment; a genuine introduction may exist in your network. None is proof of demand.
UNSURE: project dates/currentness; each contact's present role and personal pain; hospital switching intent, budget, purchasing authority and current software; Mardaleishvili scope fit; Heart Centre's present fit; Vian approval route; direct professional contact permission; primary audit details.
Unmet: 20 qualifying posts, a verified top ten and five all-PASS buyers. A shorter evidenced result is preferable to an invented list.

These are potential customers based on public signals. Check every link yourself before you reply. More precisely, this result contains a provisional research queue. AI drafts; you decide whom to contact and send.
